paper.title_en: Lepton $g-2$ non-universality of hadronic contributions and a sub-GeV window to New Physics
paper.abstract_en: We propose the linear combination of the anomalous magnetic moments of the muon and electron, $a_{μ-e} \equiv a_μ- (m_μ/m_e)^2 a_e$, as a natural low-energy window quantity that may directly probe the current discrepancy between the data-driven and lattice-QCD evaluations of hadronic contributions. The rescaling ensures an exact cancellation of the leading short-range ($m_\ell^2$-scaling) effects, thereby improving the UV behavior. Because entire classes of contributions cancel identically --- not merely in variance --- the combination is predictable in chiral perturbation theory with no free low-energy constant, and it isolates flavor-non-universal New Physics. The hadronic-vacuum-polarization effect in $a^{\rm HVP}_{μ-e}$, together with its uncertainty, is reduced as compared to $a^{\rm HVP}_μ$ by $\sim 85\%$. This is promising for tests of New Physics with some degree of flavor non-universality, conditional on significant improvements in the measurements of $a_e$ and $α$.
